results.name: Band Close Grip Row
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your palms facing each other and kept close together. Extend your arms in front of your chest, ensuring the band is taut.
Pull the handles towards your chest until your hands are close to your chest, bending your elbows and keeping them pointing outward.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you pull the handles towards your chest and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
results.description: Band Close Grip Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Band Face Pull
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight in front of you, palms facing down.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are at your face sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement, keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you pull the band towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better balance and support.
results.description: Band Face Pull is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Band Front Face Pull
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight in front of you, palms facing down.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are in front of your face.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement, keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you pull the band towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better balance and support.
results.description: Band Front Face Pull is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Band Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight down, palms facing your thighs.
Raise both handles straight in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight and palms facing down.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you raise the band handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Avoid swinging your arms; use controlled movements.
results.description: Band Front Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Upper Back.

results.name: Band Horizontal Shrug
instructions: Attach one end of a loop resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing the band with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the other end of the band with your arms extended straight forward.
Pull your shoulders backward in a horizontal shrugging motion, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
Slowly release the tension in the band, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions
tips: Focus on using your upper back and shoulders for the shrugging motion, avoiding any arm bending.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you shrug and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Use a controlled motion to ensure proper form and maximize muscle activation.
results.description: Band Horizontal Shrug is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Band Incline Row
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding one handle of the resistance band in each hand with your arms fully extended down, palms facing back. Your feet should be firm on the floor, and the resistance band should be secured under the bench.
Pull the handles towards your chest, bending your elbows and keeping them away from your body until your hands are near by your chest sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the rowing motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is secure to prevent any sudden slips.
Focus on squeezing your back muscles at the peak of the movement.
Perform each rep with controlled, deliberate movements for maximum benefit.
results.description: Band Incline Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Band Incline T Raise
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding one handle of the resistance band in each hand with your arms fully extended down, palms facing forward. Keep your feet firm on the floor and the resistance band secured under the bench.
Lift your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, forming a "T" shape with your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are parallel and your torso is stable against the bench.
Lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your arms and inhale as you lower them back down.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your neck in a neutral position by looking at the bench, not forward or down.
results.description: Band Incline T Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Band Incline Y Raise
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding one handle of the resistance band in each hand with your arms hanging down and palms facing back. Ensure the resistance band is secured under the bench.
Lift your arms diagonally in a "Y" shape until they are in line with your body, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your arms and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your shoulder joints.
results.description: Band Incline Y Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Band Reverse Fly
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold the ends of a resistance band anchored below the bench with your arms extended downward and slightly bent at the elbows, palms facing each other.
Raise your arms out to the sides in a wide arc motion until they are in line with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid joint strain and focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Ensure the bench is stable and at an appropriate incline angle to effectively target the upper back muscles.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you raise the band and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Band Reverse Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Band Seated Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under the bench with your arms hanging at your sides, palms facing inward, and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping your elbows slightly bent and leading with your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under the bench to prevent slipping.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid joint strain and focus on lifting with your shoulders.
results.description: Band Seated Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.
